anna.security: Hey team — onboarding question. We rotated our Azure Key Vault CMK (automatic key rotation) and after updating the key identifier in the Redwood console a subset of decrypts started failing with 403s. Audit in Redwood doesn't show any unwrap attempts for the affected versions. Can someone advise on likely misconfig/config gaps?

mike.s: Sorry you're hitting this. Quick questions: are you using Key Vault access policies or Azure RBAC? Which principal is Redwood using to call Key Vault (managed identity vs service principal)? And do you see any entries in the Key Vault diagnostic logs (AuditEvent)?

anna.security: We're using a service principal (appId=cc3f-xxxx). We thought we were on RBAC (we added a role earlier) but the tenant defaults still have access policies for the vault. Error when decrypting from our app: `403: Key operation 'unwrapKey' not permitted for principal 'cc3f-xxxx'`. Key Vault has automatic rotation creating a new key version. We updated the key identifier in Redwood to the new version. No AuditEvent entries for unwrapKey for that time window (checked portal).

mike.s: Two likely culprits: (1) role assignment scope — RBAC role granted at subscription/resourceGroup level won't always allow crypto ops on the key unless scoped to the vault or the key resource itself; (2) mixing access policies with RBAC can be confusing if the vault is in 'vault access policy' mode vs 'Azure RBAC' for permissions. For Key Vault crypto operations you need either an access policy with UnwrapKey/WrapKey/Get, or RBAC role like `Key Vault Crypto User` assigned at the vault or key scope for your principal.

mike.s: You can check current role assignments:```bash
az role assignment list --assignee <appId> --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault-name>
```and check access policies:```bash
az keyvault show --name <vault-name> --query properties.accessPolicies -o json
```If the role is only at subscription scope, try assigning `Key Vault Crypto User` at the vault resource or to the specific key resource (preferred).

anna.security: we ran `az role assignment list` and we do have `Key Vault Crypto User` but the scope shows the subscription (not the vault). Does that explain the 403?

mike.s: Yes — that can explain it. Crypto operations often require the role to be on the vault or the specific key. If you assign at subscription scope, Azure may not consider it applicable for key crypto ops on that vault (depends on provider). Re-assign scoped to the vault:```bash
az role assignment create --assignee <appId> --role "Key Vault Crypto User" --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault-name>
```Also ensure the principal has `get` on the key (sometimes separate).

jordan.pm: Also double-check that Key Vault diagnostic settings are enabled and sending `AuditEvent` to a workspace/storage. Many customers miss this during onboarding, so the lack of unwrap events can simply be missing diagnostics. You can enable via az:```bash
az monitor diagnostic-settings create --resource "/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault-name>" --workspace <log-analytics-id> --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'
```Once enabled, re-run the failing unwrap and look for `UnwrapKey`/`WrapKey` entries.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Ticket created: INF-2142 — assigned to eng-security and onboarding, priority P2. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-2142

sre-liz: Temporary mitigation: point Redwood back to the previous key version (if still valid) to restore decrypts while you fix role scope. If you do that, keep the old key version available for unwraps until re-wrap/rotation is completed. Also run a staging rotation test: create a new key version, assign RBAC scoped to vault for the SP, and verify `az keyvault key unwrap` using the SP creds.

anna.security: thanks — quick Q on rewrap strategy: do we need to re-wrap every existing DEK when KEK rotates, or can we leave old wrapped DEKs and keep old key versions around?

mike.s: Either approach is valid. Options: (A) Keep old KEK versions available: allow unwrap with old versions so you don't rewrap historical DEKs immediately. (B) Re-wrap DEKs proactively: create new KEK version, unwrap each DEK using old KEK and wrap with new KEK (better for forward security). For most customers we recommend rewrap during a maintenance window if you want to enforce the new KEK, otherwise keep old versions for unwrapping until data is migrated. Document that in your rotation policy.

jordan.pm: We'll add an onboarding checklist item for this customer: 1) confirm vault diagnostic `AuditEvent` enabled and connected to Redwood logging 2) ensure `Key Vault Crypto User` (or equivalent) role assigned at vault/key scope for the Redwood SP 3) verify `get`, `unwrapKey`, `wrapKey` capabilities via az or SDK 4) update Redwood console key identifier and test decrypts in staging 5) plan re-wrap or keep old versions until migration 6) record rotation schedule in tenant runbook.

anna.security: Perfect — we'll run the scoped role assignment and enable diagnostics, then update here. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

mike.s: Happy to help. If you want, drop the `az role assignment list` output here (sanitized) after the change and we can validate.

ops-bot: INF-2142 updated — waiting on customer confirmation.
